correctness.rationale: For each pair, all three vectors a,b,a+b occur as packet edge differences, giving the universal half-diameter lower bound. Integer shell separation yields the exact threshold \(2^{1/p}\), and the standard coordinate frame attains it inside a unit square. For \(p>1\) the short shell is precisely the eight nonzero {-1,0,1}^2 vectors, and the two independent configurations count 8+16 frames, all determinant one. For \(p=1\) the explicit linear isometry U=(x+y,x-y) to the planar sup norm makes each triangle circumradius half its diameter, so the three \(\ell_1\) norm inequalities are exactly necessary/sufficient. Exhausting the four unit, four diagonal, and four doubled-unit vectors gives 24+16+8=48 ordered frames, with determinant multiplicities 24 and 24. The extra vectors have even coordinate sum and determinant two, hence span the unique checkerboard index-two lattice. Standalone verify.py ran successfully on exact integer finite shells; infinite optimality is proved analytically rather than inferred from enumeration.

value.rationale: The original frame-based definition expressly allows nonbasis independent lattice vectors; deciding whether this freedom matters is structural, not a routine scalar evaluation. The natural ell_p family displays an exact boundary transition: every smoother \(p>1\) optimizer is unimodular, whereas the nonsmooth Manhattan ball has precisely twelve additional unordered index-two checkerboard minimizers despite a continuous optimum value. This complete equality classification and generator-lattice identification supplies information not contained in the previously known numerical covering minimum.
